title: MetaARIMA: Configuration-Level Transfer Learning for ARIMA Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.34171v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Time Series Foundation Models have demonstrated that pretraining on diverse datasets enables effective transfer to new forecasting tasks. Classical methods like ARIMA, however, remain configured and trained independently for each series, discarding knowledge from previous experiments. Consequently, selecting and training an ARIMA configuration remains challenging and often relies on heuristic approaches based on in-sample goodnessof-fit measures. We propose MetaARIMA, a pretrained configuration policy based on metalearning that brings transfer learning to classical statistical forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level. The policy learns from historical experiments which ARIMA configurations achieve top-quantile performance, and recommends promising candidates for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation. translated_title: MetaARIMA：面向ARIMA模型的配置级迁移学习
translated_abstract: 时间序列基础模型已经证明，在多样化数据集上进行预训练能够有效迁移到新的预测任务中。然而，像ARIMA这样的经典方法仍然需要对每个序列独立进行配置和训练，丢弃了以往实验积累的知识。因此，选择和训练ARIMA配置仍然具有挑战性，且通常依赖于基于样本内拟合优度指标的启发式方法。我们提出了MetaARIMA，这是一种基于元学习的预训练配置策略，将迁移学习引入经典统计预测中，但作用于配置层面而非模型层面。该策略从历史实验中学习哪些ARIMA配置能够达到顶尖性能水平，并为新序列推荐有前景的候选配置，同时保持可解释性和局部估计能力。在推理阶段，它通过最大边际相关性选择一组多样化的候选配置。
tldr: MetaARIMA通过元学习在配置层面（而非模型层面）为ARIMA模型引入迁移学习，从历史实验中学习高性能配置模式，为新序列推荐合适的ARIMA配置，同时保留了经典方法的可解释性和局部估计能力。
en_tdlr: MetaARIMA introduces transfer learning to classical ARIMA forecasting at the configuration level rather than the model level, using metalearning to learn from historical experiments and recommend high-performing ARIMA configurations for new series while preserving interpretability and local estimation.
